Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Summary of findings from transcript aligned with DDx:
  - Left arm numbness with subjective weakness and sensory distribution (elbow to hand), neck pain
  - Intermittent, transient left-sided visual disturbance
  - Boxing activity; symptoms progressive over ~2 weeks; partial relief with rest not observed
  - No seizures or extensive systemic symptoms reported
- Differential diagnoses considered (aligns with DDx):
  - Multiple sclerosis (MS) with demyelinating manifestations — High likelihood
  - Transient ischemic attack / amaurosis fugax — Moderate likelihood
  - Cervical radiculopathy or cervical myelopathy — Moderate likelihood
- Plan:
  - Urgent neurology referral for comprehensive evaluation and brain imaging (MRI) to assess for demyelinating disease or other CNS pathology
  - Brain imaging (MRI) as part of work-up; cervical imaging may be considered as indicated
  - No medications initiated at this visit
  - Counseling on red flags requiring immediate care: progression to leg weakness, severe headaches, vomiting, seizures, or worsening visual symptoms
  - Return or follow-up after neurology assessment to discuss results and next steps

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Multiple sclerosis (MS) with demyelinating manifestations (optic neuritis and limb sensory symptoms) — High
  - Justification: Transient monocular vision disturbance plus unilateral arm numbness/weakness in separate episodes; family autoimmune history; clinician discussion of MS and need for MRI
- Transient ischemic attack / amaurosis fugax — Moderate
  - Justification: Unilateral numbness/weakness with a transient visual disturbance; vascular etiologies considered; subacute progression over weeks
- Cervical radiculopathy / cervical spondylotic myelopathy — Moderate
  - Justification: Neck pain with unilateral arm numbness/weakness and sensory changes; boxing-related neck strain possible contributor
